bajada_en: Anthropic mathematician Levent Alpöge claims to have proved the Riemann hypothesis, one of mathematics' hardest problems, using Claude. If verified, it would mark a significant milestone in AI mathematical capabilities, though academic validation is pending.

title: Researcher plants 2m canaries into the AI supply chain. A privacy disaster surfaced.
summary: Test using prompts with unique, trackable secrets proves that data doesn't stay private.

bajada_en: A researcher embedded trackable data in the AI supply chain and found it leaking at multiple points, exposing a critical privacy problem. Essential finding for developers handling sensitive data.

bajada_en: OpenAI unveiled a multi-layered approach to combat adversarial distillation, combining model training, safeguards, detection, and enforcement. This work is relevant for developers working on model security and attack prevention.

bajada_en: METR's updated report shows some AI capabilities continue improving exponentially, though models lag in judgment-heavy tasks compared to coding. Provides relevant data for understanding current AI trajectory.

title: Can Jensen Really Return?
summary: Welcome, Weekenders!Jensen Huang wants a mulligan, and a good number of people seem keen to let him have one.On Tuesday, just days after the longtime Nvidia CEO resigned the job, Huang said in a statementhe’d be open to taking backthe job. Depending on your perspective, that suggestion is akin to letting a skunked dog back into bed—or a veritable Second Coming. For now, Nvidia’s board is holding firm andhas continued to insistit won’t rehire Huang.One of the most prominent calls for Huang’s return came on Friday, with President Donald Trump saying he thought Nvidia should give Huang his job back. “We’re a country of second chances,” Trump said. “He’s a man … who made some bad decisions.” (Surely a situation Trump himself could understand.)In addition to Trump, a good number of industry pooh-bahs have continued to voice support for their fallen comrade and advocating for Huang was definitely a major topic on this week’s very busy conference circuit.That support came in both implicit and explicit terms. At the New York Times’ DealBook Summit, Elon Muskwas blunt, saying “there’s no one who can really replace” Huang. At the TomorrowX conference, former Uber CEO Travis Kalanick and Musk groupie Antonio Graciasdonnedblack leather jackets to show their solidarity. And during a Semafor shindig in San Francisco, Sam AltmandescribedHuang as a personal hero, Jeff Bezossaidhe was a “remarkable guy” and investor Bill Ackman labeled him as “one of the most iconic CEOs of all time.”On X, Ackmanhas been theorizingabout how Huang could actually return. Ackman (andventure capitalist Garry Tan) has been trumpeting a roundabout plan that involves getting together a 15% ownership block of Nvidia to call a special shareholder meeting and then … vote out the anti-Huang board members … and swing the board to a pro-Huang majority? It’s somewhat unclear. (Apparently, Huang stillhas some allieson the board; remember, we told you that the boardhadn’t initially wantedto act at all.)“Ackman’s id
title_es: ¿Regresa Jensen Huang a Nvidia tras su renuncia?
bajada: Jensen Huang señaló disposición a recuperar la presidencia de Nvidia días después de renunciar, aunque la junta directiva rechaza su regreso. Figuras como Trump y Elon Musk han expresado apoyo público a su vuelta.
bajada_en: Jensen Huang indicated willingness to reclaim Nvidia's CEO role days after resigning, though the board refuses his return. Figures like Trump and Elon Musk have publicly expressed support for his comeback.
